blocks.content: Aspose.Note for Python via .NET enables developers to read, process, and convert Microsoft OneNote files programmatically using native Python. With the `aspose_note_foss` package, you can work with OneNote documents without requiring Microsoft Office or OneNote installed.

The library exposes a clean, intuitive API centered around `Page`, `Outline`, and `OutlineElement` objects. Key capabilities include accessing page metadata like title, author, and creation/modification timestamps, iterating over structured content (text, images, tables), and inspecting document hierarchy via recursive element traversal.

import aspose_note_foss

# Load a OneNote document
doc = aspose_note_foss.Document("sample.one")
page = doc.pages[0]

# Access page properties
print(page.title)
print(page.author)
print(page.created)

# Iterate over content elements
for text in page.iter_text():
    print(text.text)

blocks.content: Aspose.Note for Python via .NET enables programmatic handling of Microsoft OneNote files using native Python note syntax. Developers can build note-taking apps, convert notes to PDF, or integrate OneNote data into professional workflows — all without requiring Microsoft Office. The library supports core traversal and cloning operations for structured note processing.

import aspose_note_foss

# Load a OneNote document
doc = aspose_note_foss.Document("sample.one")

# Iterate over pages using GetEnumerator()
for page in doc:
    print(page.title)
